answer: Bind each identity to one airline loyalty account with at least four verified flown segments, attested by the airline, so a single traveler can hold only one qualifying history. Like a comet leaving one trail, each account's flights form a single trace; a prism of fare, route and date checks exposes any bought account when the names mismatch. Forging 1,000 identities means actually flying 4,000 segments, roughly $400,000 in the cheapest fares, while an honest agent pays for its own trips once. The whisper of a limit: it excludes people who never fly, and airlines must expose the check.
